assessment.security_status_en: The security situation in the region remains highly tense after Saudi air defenses successfully intercepted another Houthi missile over Riyadh. Attacks in the Red Sea and surrounding strategic corridors continue to disrupt international trade and pose a direct risk to global energy stability.

assessment.forecast_review_en: The previous forecast was fully confirmed as persistent incidents in key corridors continue to drive up oil prices and maintain high nervousness across financial markets.

articles.title: Centcom rejects Iran's claims on warship attack, Hormuz shipping charges
articles.summary:
Centcom rejects Iran's claims on warship attack, Hormuz shipping charges

The United States Central Command (Centcom) has refuted the Iranian military's claim that Iran attacked the USS Abraham Lincoln on the first day of the war, or that the IRGC regained control of two Iranian oil tankers seized by the US forces.

In a post on X, Centcom also refuted Iran's charge that it was charging $2.5 million from ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

An Iranian military commander made multiple FALSE claims concerning U.S. Forces over the past 24 hours: 🚫 CLAIM: The U.S. military stole two Iranian oil tankers and the IRGC’s navy retook the vessels while American troops on board slept. ✅ FACT: Iran no longer has a navy. The entire situation the Iranian military commander described is another fabricated lie. 🚫 CLAIM: Iranian naval forces struck aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72) on the first day of Operation Epic Fury, forcing U.S. forces to seek assistance from regional countries for evacuation support. ✅ FACT: The Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group was well defended and never struck by Iran as a result. In fact, the strike group completed a historically successful combat deployment to the Middle East and safely returned to the United States last month. 🚫 CLAIM: CENTCOM is charging $2.5 million to ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. ✅ FACT: While U.S. forces and regional partners do control the Strait of Hormuz, there is no toll for passing ships. CENTCOM’s efforts have restored freedom of navigation through the international waterway. Thousands of ships and billions of crude oil barrels have transited the strait freely and safely under U.S. protection despite unwarranted Iranian aggression.

— U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM) November 28, 2026

Saudi air defences destroy Houthi cruise missile over Riyadh

Saudi Arabia’s air defences have intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by Yemen’s Houthis towards Riyadh, Major General Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition forces, said on X.

Meanwhile, Houthi-affiliated Al Masirah TV reported that Saudi air strikes have targeted telecommunications networks in the districts of al-Sawma’ah, Mukayras and the rural areas of al-Bayda governorate.

articles.title: Houthi attacks kill three civilians and wound three others in Taiz, report says
articles.summary:
Houthi attacks kill three civilians and wound three others in Taiz, report says

Houthi attacks in Yemen's Taiz province killed three civilians, including a child, according to the government-run Saba news agency.

Houthi drone strikes, rocket fire and sniper attacks targeted residential areas on Friday, killing three people, including a 10-year-old boy and his father, the report said.

Among the injured was an 18-month-old girl, who was wounded in shelling in the Sabir al-Mawadim district.

articles.title: Yemeni forces claim 121 Houthi fighters killed in 726 attacks
articles.summary:
Yemeni forces claim 121 Houthi fighters killed in 726 attacks

Colonel Majed al-Nuzaili, spokesman for Yemen’s government forces, claimed as many as 726 attacks had been carried against Houthi positions over the past 24 hours.

Al-Nuzaili said the operations, conducted as part of the “Dawn of Yemen” offensive, included 23 air strikes, 642 artillery attacks, 35 drone operations and 26 rocket strikes. They resulted in the killing or wounding 121 fighters and commanders, according to the state-run Saba news agency.

The attacks also destroyed or damaged 81 military vehicles and pieces of equipment, he added.

articles.title: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview reveals naive bias in handling of Putin’s aggression
articles.summary:
Trump’s son-in-law and senior negotiator paints Russian invasion of Ukraine as a misunderstanding to be resolved

In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars.

During the conversation this week with Mathias Döpfner, the chief executive of the Axel Springer media publisher, Kushner gave a rare insight into his diplomatic technique, offering a string of homilies that veered close to banalities: “You have nothing until you have something”, “diplomacy is like untying knots on a fishing line for his son”, and “you play the ball from where it lands”.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea are expected, keeping energy prices and shipping volatility high. Markets will remain sensitive to any news regarding military retaliation.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu se dramaticky vyhrotila po útoku Houthiů na saúdské ropné rafinerie a zprávách o úderech na tankery v Hormuzském průlivu. Konflikt se nadále šíří, doprovázen raketovými útoky v Saúdské Arábii a eskalací bojů v Jemenu.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region has escalated dramatically following Houthi attacks on Saudi oil refineries and reports of strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. archive.forecast_en: Extreme volatility in oil and commodity prices is expected over the coming days due to direct attacks on energy infrastructure, with markets remaining highly sensitive to any signs of military retaliation.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu a Rudého moře se prudce vyhrotila po útocích na energetickou infrastrukturu a tankery, včetně výbuchu LNG nosiče po nástraze miny.
